body:
Docs jobs for different PRs, the deploy from `main`, and the preview cleanup all push to `gh-pages`. When another job moves `gh-pages` between the clone and the push, Documenter's `--force-with-lease` push is refused and the docs job fails, as on #827 and #831.

`docs/make.jl` now retries `deploydocs` up to ten times with a random delay of 10 to 30 s (cloning `gh-pages`, amending, then force-pushing currently takes about 40s). This lets deployments recover from races.


Nearly half of the 40s it takes cloning `gh-pages` and pushing can be attributed to the `push` step. I _think_ the push is slow because each deploy creates a commit without a parent, so GitHub checks the whole tree of about 19,000 files instead of only the changed ones.

`DocCleanup.yml` is intended to delete doc previews for closed PRs, but races and other issues have led to 29 of the 43 previews on `gh-pages` belonging to closed PRs. This job runs every time a PR is closed. Previously it would only (attempt to) clean up its own preview. Now it also checks if other previews can be pruned.

To further reduce the size of `gh-pages`, the doc-cleanup job also replaces patch releases that aren't the latest patch with a symlink to the latest (e.g., if I publish `v0.41.1`, `v0.41.0` will now point to the contents of `v0.41.1`).

The cleanup job edits a temporary index instead of checking out `gh-pages`, and pushes with `--force-with-lease` and the same retry; the previous cleanup pushed with `--force`, which could overwrite a concurrent deploy.

A dry run against a copy of `gh-pages` took 3 s and reduced the checked-out tree from 4.6 GB to 1.7 GB, with no dangling symlinks. A local test with a concurrent push confirmed that the retry keeps the other commit.

---

Before writing this PR, I checked if ClimaAtmos does anything smarter, but alas, no.
title: fix(docs): retry gh-pages pushes and prune gh-pages on PR close
